statements.text: Today, AI searches consume nearly 10 times the electricity of standard internet searches. [...] Analysts predict this could climb to as much as 12 percent by 2030.
statements.context: Floor speech in the House of Representatives during a grid reliability discussion, announcing the member's plan to create an AI and Energy Working Group.

statements.text: I agree with Mr. Connaughton that this could—AI could drive or power the fourth Industrial Revolution in our country. But in order to do that, we need to power AI. And meeting the energy demands of this business are—that is a substantial challenge for our country. It is why I launched an AI and Energy Working Group this week, and invite you all to participate.
statements.context: The speaker is participating in a congressional hearing on brownfields redevelopment and innovation, steering the discussion toward AI energy demands.

statements.text: We have got a working group my office has led on AI and energy. We want to try to get some solutions and a policy framework for solutions to bring to the table on this very issue.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on the economics of AI, data centers, and power consumption.

statements.text: When I look back on the 12 years as a regulator in my state— and we served during a time of energy boom, so we saw demand increase—it was still like 3 percent. [...] they said that their peak demand today is 150 gigawatts and they are looking in 5 years to be at 185 gigawatts. That is mind- blowing. That is astounding.
statements.context: Rep. Fedorchak, a freshman House member, speaks as a guest in a Senate hearing on AI, data centers, and power consumption, asking expert witnesses about efficiency upgrades.

statements.text: So AI has been described as not only a powerful tool, but an incredible weapon. [...] given that China today produces 10,000 terawat hours of power a year and the U.S. produces 4,000 terawat hours of power a year, we are already quite behind.
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI applications in communications and technology, with the chair recognizing herself to question a witness.

statements.text: So AI has been described as not only a powerful tool but an incredible weapon. [...] we are already quite behind. [...] what barriers is China facing in their deployment of AI?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI applications in communications and technology, where the lawmaker questions a witness about the U.S.–China AI competitive gap.

statements.text: I am very concerned about having the power to meet the demand of the moment for AI, and so my office is leading an AI energy working group, and I would invite all of you to participate in it.
statements.context: Remarks by Mrs. Fedorchak during a congressional panel discussion on AI applications in communications and technology.

statements.text: Are there emerging AI-related vulnerabilities? And how are you using AI to both detect and recover? And what other vulnerabilities are being created by AI?
statements.context: Question posed during a Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee hearing on securing America's energy infrastructure.
